skill.name: shopify-development
skill.description: Build Shopify apps, UI extensions, themes, and API integrations with guidance for Shopify CLI, GraphQL Admin API, Polaris, Liquid, webhooks, billing, and metafields.
skill.summary: Develop Shopify apps, extensions, themes, and API workflows with practical templates and helper scripts.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation or test false positives from Markdown backticks, Liquid syntax, placeholder URLs, and dummy credentials. The real risks are in optional helper scripts that read local credentials, load parent .env files, write API keys into generated configuration, and send access tokens to a caller-controlled Shopify host.

remediation.issue: Parent .env files are discovered and parsed by the initializer.
remediation.suggestion: Limit credential loading to an explicit project-local path, or require user confirmation before reading parent agent or skills directories.

remediation.issue: Generated shopify.app.toml can include a real Shopify API key.
remediation.suggestion: Write placeholders by default and document how users should provide credentials through local untracked environment files.

remediation.issue: GraphQL helper accepts arbitrary shop domains before sending access tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Validate that shop domains match expected Shopify host patterns, and reject URLs with paths, ports, credentials, or non-Shopify domains.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts use local credentials and outbound network access.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit runtime warnings, dry-run behavior, and documentation that explains what secrets and network destinations are used.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated API Host Receives Access Token
semantic_findings.description: ShopifyGraphQL accepts a shop_domain string, strips only the scheme, builds a URL from it, and later sends X-Shopify-Access-Token to that host. A hostile or mistyped domain could receive an Admin API token.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly combines caller-controlled shop_domain with the token-bearing request header. The risk depends on caller input, but the unsafe trust boundary is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Parent Environment Files Can Populate Generated Config
semantic_findings.description: The initializer searches .env files in the skill, parent skills directory, and parent agent directory, then can place the configured Shopify API key into generated shopify.app.toml content. This can propagate secrets outside their original storage location.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file discovery, credential loading, and generated config write are all present in the script. The exposure requires running the helper, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.user_title: Build Shopify Apps, Extensions, and Themes
content.value_statement: Shopify development spans apps, extensions, APIs, themes, and compliance details. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused patterns for real Shopify work.
actual_capabilities: Routes requests toward Shopify apps, UI extensions, theme work, or combined app and theme extension builds.
Provides Shopify CLI commands for app setup, extension generation, theme previews, and deployment workflows.
Includes GraphQL Admin API examples for products, orders, customers, metafields, billing, webhooks, and rate limits.
Covers checkout, admin, POS, customer account, and Shopify Function extension patterns.
Supplies Liquid theme examples for sections, snippets, product forms, cart behavior, and storefront assets.
Includes Python helper scripts for project initialization and Shopify GraphQL API calls.
limitations: Examples target Shopify API version 2026-01 and should be checked before production release.
Helper scripts require Python, Shopify CLI, and valid Shopify credentials when used locally.
The skill does not replace Shopify app review, privacy review, or compliance review.
Reference code still needs project-specific authentication, validation, logging, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Plan an Embedded Shopify App
use_cases.description: Use OAuth, scopes, GraphQL, webhook, billing, and project structure guidance to design an app implementation.

use_cases.title: Build Storefront Theme Features
use_cases.description: Use Liquid, sections, snippets, product forms, and cart patterns to customize storefront behavior.

use_cases.title: Create Commerce UI Extensions
use_cases.description: Use checkout, admin, POS, customer account, and Function examples to plan targeted merchant experiences.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Shopify Build Type
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to build a Shopify feature for [goal]. Decide whether this should be an app, extension, theme change, or combined approach.

prompt_templates.title: Design an App Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Shopify app that uses [data or workflow]. Include scopes, OAuth flow, webhooks, GraphQL operations, and deployment steps.

prompt_templates.title: Implement an Extension Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Shopify [checkout, admin, POS, or customer account] extension for [merchant task]. Include target, data needs, UI flow, and API calls.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Shopify Build
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Shopify implementation plan for security, API limits, webhooks, billing, theme impact, and app review readiness.

output_examples.input: User asks how to add a gift message to checkout.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a checkout UI extension, identifies the target, lists required state, and describes attribute update behavior.

output_examples.input: User asks how to sync products from Shopify.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines GraphQL product queries, pagination, scopes, rate limit handling, and webhook updates for changed products.

output_examples.input: User asks how to customize a product page.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests Liquid section and snippet changes, product form considerations, image handling, and theme preview steps.

best_practices: Request the smallest Shopify access scopes that support the feature.
Validate webhook HMAC signatures and OAuth state values before processing requests.
Check Shopify API versions and GraphQL query costs before production deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode merchant credentials, access tokens, or secrets in app or theme files.
Do not build checkout changes as theme code when Shopify requires an extension.
Do not process large stores without pagination, retries, and rate limit handling.

faq.question: What Shopify work does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports apps, UI extensions, themes, GraphQL Admin API work, webhooks, billing, metafields, and Shopify Functions.

faq.question: Does it include executable code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Python helper scripts for project initialization and GraphQL calls, plus tests for the initializer.

faq.question: Can it help with Shopify CLI workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common Shopify CLI commands for apps, extensions, themes, previews, and deployments.

faq.question: Does it validate Shopify credentials?
faq.answer: No. Users must provide valid credentials and handle credential storage securely in their own environment.

faq.question: Is the reference code production ready?
faq.answer: No. It is a starting point and needs project-specific validation, security checks, logging, and tests.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
